meta.description: Loads mass-spectrometry data into Python/R and strips the search engine's bookkeeping before any number is trusted -- removes decoys (REV__/Reverse), contaminants (CON__/Potential contaminant), Only-identified-by-site groups, and resolves semicolon razor/leading protein-ID ambiguity in MaxQuant proteinGroups.txt, DIA-NN report.parquet, and mzML/mzXML. Distinguishes Intensity (raw) vs LFQ intensity (MaxLFQ) vs iBAQ, treats a MaxQuant zero as missing (NaN, not log2(-inf)), and diagnoses the missingness contract (intensity-dependent in both DDA and DIA; DIA has fewer missing values). Use when starting an analysis from raw spectra or a search engine output. Downstream normalization and stats are differential-abundance; reporter-ion/MaxLFQ quant is quantification; protein grouping is protein-inference.
meta.environment: pyOpenMS 3.5.0; pandas 3.0.5; numpy 2.5.3; R 4.4.3 with QFeatures 1.16.0; DIA-NN 2.6.1 Academia and msconvert 3.0.26253 (to produce the real inputs) (F:/OpenScience/audit-envs/mass-spec-proteomics-analyst)
meta.data: SYNTHETIC: proteinGroups.txt (1560 rows, 8 LFQ runs), proteinGroups_failed.txt (Intensity/iBAQ/LFQ families, one weak run T4), report.parquet (8 runs, 60 LOWCONF groups), synthetic_mixed.mzML (DDA + DIA + offsets-missing + all-ion scans, with a truth table), MaxQuant TMT10 proteinGroups.txt and FragPipe combined_protein.tsv (rerun/make_new_tables.py). PUBLIC: PXD070049 (CC0, Van Puyvelde 2026) Orbitrap Astral 5-min 250 pg -- one DIA mzML (20,409 spectra) and a real DIA-NN 2.6.1 report.parquet.

skill_veto.detail: Every Skill code block ran to completion on the inputs it is scoped for (MaxQuant proteinGroups.txt, DIA-NN report.parquet, mzML) including a real 20,409-spectrum Astral file and a real DIA-NN 2.6.1 report. No loops, no nondeterminism (same shapes and counts on repeat runs). The two failures observed are on tables outside the Skill's declared formats (FragPipe) or outside its documented quant column family (MaxQuant TMT), and both are recorded as recommendations, not stability failures. Code is read-only on user data.

scientific_integrity.detail: Six references, all real and now correctly attributed (the pyOpenMS misattribution to Chambers 2012 is fixed; Rost 2014 Proteomics 14(1):74-77 is cited). No invented numbers. Every synthetic dataset is labelled SYNTHETIC in the scripts that make and use it.

practice_boundaries.detail: No diagnostic, prescriptive or triage content anywhere; the Skill only imports and characterises data.

methodological_ground.detail: The missingness teaching is now correct and was confirmed on real data: on a real Astral DIA matrix the abundance-missingness correlation is -0.444 and missingness runs 29.8% in the lowest abundance quartile against 1.7% in the highest -- exactly the intensity-dependent structure the fixed text describes. The Intensity / LFQ intensity / iBAQ distinction was confirmed against a table with a deliberate loading failure.

code_usability.detail: All four code blocks ran verbatim under pandas 3.0.5 / numpy 2.5.3 / pyOpenMS 3.5.0 on the formats the Skill declares, on both synthetic and real files, with no syntax errors, no missing imports and no -inf.

functional_suitability.note: Completeness 3, Correctness 3, Appropriateness 4. All five pass-1 correctness defects are fixed and each was re-verified by execution: Global.PG.Q.Value in the DIA filter, 0 -> NaN in the DIA block, the DIA-MCAR claim replaced with a diagnostic-driven one, the mzML precursor guard, and the pyOpenMS citation. Still incomplete: no TMT route at all although the taxonomy claims TMT coverage, and the R/QFeatures route is named with no code (left unfixed as new content).

reliability.note: Fault tolerance 3, Error reporting 3, Recoverability 4. The block now raises on a table with no LFQ columns, drops all-NaN rows, skips precursor-less MS2 scans and prints a named warning when isolation offsets are absent -- all four confirmed. Two gaps left: the no-LFQ error message points a TMT user at Intensity columns that do not exist in a TMT proteinGroups.txt, and the three-way .get() flag mask collapses to a scalar when all three flag columns are absent, producing `KeyError: True`.

performance_context.note: Token cost 3, Execution efficiency 4. ~19 KB single file, all inline. The code is linear and fast: 20,409 real spectra parsed in 16 s, a 46k-row DIA-NN report reduced to a matrix in well under a second.

agent_usability.note: Learnability 3, Consistency 4, Feedback design 3, Error prevention 4. The DIA q-value filter now agrees with the sibling dia-analysis Skill (both name Global.PG.Q.Value and the 1.9.x Lib.* alternative), zero handling is stated for MaxQuant and DIA-NN alike, and the >=2-peptide threshold row now says explicitly that the import code does not apply it. All other floors are met: static 84 >= 80, execution 86.0 >= 85, Layer 1 35.6/40 >= 32, Layer 2 50.4/60 >= 48.
final.delta_vs_pre_fix: 78 Beta Only (not deployable) -> 85.2 Limited Release (deployable). All four pre-fix P1 findings and two of three P2 findings are confirmed fixed by execution; the QFeatures P2 was deliberately left, and three new defects were found by inputs the fixer was not told about (TMT, a flagless table, and the degenerate mask behind it).

key_strengths: Every pass-1 P1 fix was re-verified by running the Skill's own code, not by reading the diff: 0/60 LOWCONF groups now survive the DIA filter, 0 -inf anywhere, the mzML loop completes over an all-ion scan and names the scan whose offsets are missing, and the all-NaN rows are gone.

The rewritten missingness teaching is correct on real data, which is the strongest single result in this audit: on a real Orbitrap Astral DIA matrix the correlation is -0.444 and missingness runs 29.8% in the lowest abundance quartile against 1.7% in the highest.

The quant-column teaching is demonstrably right: on a table with a deliberate loading failure, the weak run sits 1.33 log2 low in Intensity and iBAQ and exactly 0.00 in LFQ intensity, and iBAQ carries raw Intensity's between-sample ratios identically (SD 0.0).
The DIA filter is now consistent with the sibling dia-analysis Skill, so an agent running both does not get two different definitions of 1% FDR.
The blocks scale: 20,409 real spectra parsed in 16 s with zero spurious warnings, and a 46k-row real DIA-NN report reduced to a matrix in under a second.

recommendations.title: No TMT route, and the no-LFQ error sends a TMT user to columns that do not exist
recommendations.problem: On a MaxQuant TMT10 proteinGroups.txt the block raises 'No LFQ intensity columns: LFQ was not enabled in MaxQuant; use Intensity and normalize explicitly'. A TMT proteinGroups.txt has no per-sample 'Intensity <sample>' columns -- only one summed 'Intensity' column -- so the suggested fallback is a dead end. The channels are in 'Reporter intensity corrected 1..N'. The Tool Taxonomy claims MaxQuant txt output covers 'DDA label-free / TMT search results' but no decision-tree row, code block or threshold mentions reporter ions.
recommendations.root_cause: The block and its new error message were written for the label-free case only, while the taxonomy advertises TMT.
recommendations.fix: Add a decision-tree row 'MaxQuant TMT / isobaric labelling -> read Reporter intensity corrected <n> columns; corrected channels apply MaxQuant's isotope-impurity correction, uncorrected do not; reporter-ion quant computation itself is quantification', and change the ValueError to name the columns the table actually has, e.g. 'No LFQ intensity columns. Found Reporter intensity corrected columns -> this is an isobaric (TMT/iTRAQ) run; see the TMT row. Otherwise use Intensity and normalize explicitly.'

recommendations.title: The flag-column guard collapses to a scalar when all three flag columns are absent
recommendations.problem: `mask = (pg.get('Reverse','') != '+') & (pg.get('Potential contaminant','') != '+') & (pg.get('Only identified by site','') != '+')` returns a Series while at least one flag column is present, but the Python bool True when all three are absent; `pg[True]` then raises `KeyError: True`. The Common Errors table recommends exactly this .get() pattern as the guard for a missing flag column, so the Skill documents a guard that does not hold in the case it is meant for.
recommendations.root_cause: pandas `.get(col, '')` returns the scalar default, and `'' != '+'` is a bool, not a Series; the failure only surfaces when no flag column survives to keep the expression a Series.
recommendations.fix: Build the mask from a Series of the right length, e.g. `mask = pd.Series(True, index=pg.index)` then `for c in ('Reverse','Potential contaminant','Only identified by site'): mask &= pg.get(c, pd.Series('', index=pg.index)) != '+'`, and raise a named error when none of the three columns is present ('no MaxQuant flag columns found -- is this a proteinGroups.txt?'). Correct the Common Errors row to match.

recommendations.title: R/QFeatures route is named with no code, and the obvious call fails on MaxQuant column names
recommendations.problem: The decision tree routes R pipelines to `readQFeatures` + `aggregateFeatures` and the taxonomy prefers QFeatures over MSnbase, but the Skill ships no R code. readQFeatures 1.16.0 works, but `filterFeatures` with the MaxQuant names as written errors ('Potential contaminant' is/are absent from all rowData) because readQFeatures applies make.names(), turning the spaces into dots. An agent hits this on the first try. (The fix log records this as deliberately deferred: adding a QFeatures block is new content.)
recommendations.root_cause: The R route was documented from package names rather than from a run.
recommendations.fix: Add a short R block: `readQFeatures(assayData=..., quantCols=..., runCol=...)`, then `filterFeatures(~ Reverse != '+')`, `filterFeatures(~ Potential.contaminant != '+')`, `filterFeatures(~ Only.identified.by.site != '+')` with a one-line note that readQFeatures renames columns via make.names(), then `zeroIsNA()` and `logTransform()`. Verified working shape on the audit table: 1500 x 8, no -Inf, 19.8% NA.

recommendations.title: Only one runnable example, and it covers the block that changed least
recommendations.problem: examples/ ships load_maxquant.py only. The DIA-NN and mzML blocks are the two that changed most in pass 1 and neither has an example or any test input, so a regression in either is invisible until a user hits it.
recommendations.fix: Add examples/load_diann.py and examples/load_mzml.py with a few-hundred-row synthetic report.parquet and a ~20-spectrum mzML that includes one all-ion scan and one scan with missing isolation offsets, so both guards are exercised by running the example.

recommendations.title: The cleaning blocks do not report what they removed
recommendations.problem: The MaxQuant and DIA blocks silently drop rows. An agent following the Skill hands the user a matrix with no record of how many bookkeeping rows, sub-threshold rows or all-NaN rows were removed, which is exactly the provenance a methods section needs.
recommendations.root_cause: The blocks are written as minimal transformations.
recommendations.fix: Add one print per block summarising rows read, rows removed by each criterion, and final matrix shape, and say in the Approach text that this line belongs in the methods record.
